title: Select [CASE WHEN - Shorthand]
description:
## CASE Shorthand
When you're checking the same column every time, there's a shorter syntax:
```sql
-- Long form
CASE
    WHEN status = 'running' THEN 'ok'
    WHEN status = 'stopped' THEN 'down'
END

-- Shorthand
CASE status
    WHEN 'running' THEN 'ok'
    WHEN 'stopped' THEN 'down'
END
```
You can also use CASE to change what VALUE a column shows based on conditions.


---
## Assignment:
BWS needs a cost report. Select each server's name and a cost column:
- status is 'running' -> show cpu_cores * 10 (active cost)
- status is 'on fire' -> show cpu_cores * 25 (emergency cost)
- anything else -> show 0
setupCode: CREATE TABLE servers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, cpu_cores INTEGER, status TEXT); INSERT INTO servers VALUES (1, 'prod-1', 8, 'running'), (2, 'prod-2', 16, 'running'), (3, 'staging-1', 4, 'stopped'), (4, 'dev-box', 2, 'on fire'), (5, 'test', 1, 'pending');
expectedOutput:
name | cost
prod-1 | 80
prod-2 | 160
staging-1 | 0
dev-box | 50
test | 0
